You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is the source mug visibly positioned to the right of the same headphones, is there reliable evidence of relevant attempted movement without fulfillment, is there reliable evidence that no relevant progress occurred, or is the result unresolved?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Fail only when visual evidence reliably establishes that no relevant progress toward moving the source mug occurred. Evidence of attempted movement without fulfillment is also fail for this required condition. Assess the source mug's former location and the edited scene for evidence of attempted movement, but do not infer progress from blue color alone, from the presence of a right-side mug, or from unrelated or newly generated mugs. A remnant counts as evidence of attempted movement only when its shape, position, and appearance reliably connect it to the source mug. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish fulfillment or whether relevant progress occurred.
node.binding: Compare the source image's large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with each edited mug, allowing for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting; compare the same headphones and assess whether the source mug is to their right. Explicitly inspect the source mug's former location and the surrounding edited scene: assess the remnant's position, outline, and appearance, and whether these together with other visible changes reliably indicate attempted movement of the source mug. Do not treat color alone, an indistinct blur, or a different-looking mug as proof of identity or progress. Keep attempted movement distinct from fulfillment; retain unresolved if identity or movement cannot reliably be established.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a large light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a mug is to the right of the headphones, but it looks different from the source mug; another mug appears left of the headphones, and the source mug's former location is only an indistinct blue blur. The blur and visible mugs do not reliably establish whether the source mug was moved, so neither fulfillment nor relevant attempted movement can be confirmed.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s conservative identity test is appropriate, but it collapses visible partial progress into unknown. The edited image shows the original mug’s former left-side area as a conspicuous blue blur, while mugs appear on both sides of the headphones; this is evidence of an attempted edit, though not reliable proof that the right-side mug is the source mug or that the move was completed. Clarify the decision boundary so a clearly relevant but incomplete/identity-uncertain edit can be distinguished from no progress, while retaining unknown when even attempted movement cannot be established. Do not infer source-mug identity from color or the right-side mug alone. The trace is valid and has no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the mismatch is semantic/criterion calibration, not a reason to force the reference label. Also avoid treating high confidence in an unresolved judgment as evidence that the requested edit is absent."}
